The feeder column is a numeric technical identifier for a distribution feeder in the electrical grid. While it is a quasi-identifier that, combined with substation, narrows down a geographic area, it does not directly identify any natural person. With 70+ housing units per feeder, re-identification of an individual is highly unlikely. It is infrastructure metadata, not personal data under GDPR/DPV.

Similar to feeder, the substation is a numeric identifier for grid infrastructure. It serves as a quasi-identifier for location but does not constitute personal data. The aggregation level (70+ units) makes individual re-identification impractical. No direct link to a natural person exists.

The date column contains temporal information (e.g., 2023-04-01). It is a standard time reference for load data and does not identify any individual. While it could be part of a temporal re-identification chain when combined with other datasets, on its own it carries negligible privacy risk for aggregate feeder-level data.

This is an aggregate count of housing units (70-72) within a feeder area. It is statistical/aggregate data, not personal data. The count is sufficiently large to prevent re-identification of specific households. It provides context for load calculations but does not expose individual information.

This is an aggregate count of industrial and commercial units (11) in the feeder area. It is statistical data at the infrastructure level. While a small number, it does not identify specific businesses or individuals. It serves as a denominator for load distribution calculations.

This is the total installed capacity (kW) of storage heaters across all consumers in the feeder. It is purely aggregate technical data with no link to any individual. The value (144.4 kW) represents a sum across 70+ units, making individual attribution impossible.

Total installed capacity of heat pumps in the feeder area. Aggregate technical infrastructure data with no personal data component. The value (2.1 kW) is a sum across multiple consumers and cannot be traced to any individual.

Total installed capacity of electric heaters in the feeder. Purely aggregate technical data. No personal identifiers or individual-level information is present. The value represents a collective measurement.

Total installed capacity of hot water tanks in the feeder area. Aggregate technical data with no personal data. The value (6.0 kW) is a sum across many consumers and cannot identify any individual household.

Total installed capacity of EV chargers in the feeder area. Aggregate technical data. The value (0.0 kW) indicates no EV chargers are registered. No personal data is exposed, and the zero value provides no identifying information.

Total installed capacity of public lighting in the feeder area. This is municipal/infrastructure data, not personal data. The value (10.0 kW) represents public assets and has no connection to any individual's privacy.

Total installed capacity of other/miscellaneous consumers in the feeder. Aggregate technical data with no personal data component. The value (254.5 kW) is a collective sum that cannot be attributed to any specific individual or business.

Feeder is an infrastructure identifier that does not directly identify a natural person. Under DPV it is considered non‑personal technical metadata, so anonymisation is not required.
Substation is a utility asset identifier. It is not personal data and cannot be used to single out an individual without additional linking information.
A calendar date alone is not personal data. Even combined with other non‑personal columns it does not uniquely identify a person, so no anonymisation is needed.

The count of housing units is an aggregated statistic. While it could be a quasi‑identifier in very small areas, the dataset aggregates at the feeder/substation level, making re‑identification unlikely. Hence anonymisation is not required.
